topDriver: AMD +18% post-blowout + Arm Q4 record + Iran peace memorandum imminent: AI hardware supercycle and geopolitical de-escalation converging in a single session.
narrativeSummary: May 6 was one of the most explosive sessions of 2026, combining the most powerful AI hardware earnings week in history with the most credible Iran peace signal yet. The session opened with AMD gapping up 18% after its Tuesday AH blowout — the data center +57% print crystallised into the broadest chip rally in months. Arm's intraday +13.6% (ahead of its own record-breaking AH results) and Corning's +12% on a $500M Nvidia AI-infrastructure optical networking deal confirmed the AI hardware trade is now spanning the complete stack: CPU architecture (ARM), AI GPU/CPU (AMD), memory (MU), optical networking (GLW), and foundry (INTC/TSMC). The session's other engine was the Iran peace signal. Axios reported the White House believed it was close to a one-page memorandum de-escalating the conflict, after Trump paused 'Project Freedom' — the Hormuz escort mission — to allow room for diplomacy. WTI fell nearly 7% to $95.19, the first sub-$96 close since before the Iran war began in earnest. Brent dropped below $100. The S&P Energy sector fell over 4% as oil sold off. Gold surged +2.89% to $4,700 as the dollar weakened, paradoxically benefiting from both the safe-haven unwind (Iran resolution = geopolitical premium reduced, but dollar falls more) and the stagflation/fiscal premium. The 10Y fell 6.8bps to 4.348% as oil's inflation signal dimmed. After the bell, Arm delivered exactly what the market needed: record Q4 revenue $1.49B (+20%), EPS $0.60, license revenue +29%, data center royalties more than doubled, AGI CPU demand 'exceeded expectations.' ARM laid out a $15B chip revenue target by 2031 and >$9 EPS. Stock +12.6% AH to $267. The AI infrastructure trade now has a five-year roadmap backed by confirmed quarterly revenue.
macroStressSubtext: Iran peace memorandum imminent + WTI sub-$96 + records across indices drops MSI from High to Elevated. Warsh, fiscal 30Y, and Hormuz formal reopening outstanding.
rateCurveRead: The curve rallied sharply on May 6 — the 10Y fell 6.8bps to 4.35% and the 30Y retreated from its 5.02% (2007 high) back to 4.98% as WTI's near-7% collapse removed the most acute inflationary pressure from the long end. The Iran peace memorandum signal was the primary driver: if Hormuz reopens, energy inflation resolves and the long-end premium compresses. The 2Y fell 2bps to 3.93%, keeping the 2/10 spread at +42bps — narrowing slightly from yesterday's +50bps. The bear-steepener is pausing, not reversing. Even with today's rally, the 10Y remains elevated at 4.35% and the 30Y above 4.98% — the fiscal risk premium does not fully resolve with a Hormuz peace deal alone. Source: Federal Reserve H.15 official May 6, 2026 release.

flowsRead: May 6 flows tell a binary story: everything AI and everything Iran-resolution is being bought, everything oil-and-inflation-hedge is being sold. The $5.2B semiconductor inflow is the session's defining move — AMD's 18% gap-up alone represented $50B+ in market cap creation. The $2.9B energy outflow is the inflation-trade reversal: WTI sub-$96 is a game-changer for the PCE trajectory if sustained. Gold's $1.4B inflow is the unusual signal — gold is not de-escalating, it is re-positioning. As USD weakens on the Iran deal, gold picks up the store-of-value premium that oil was carrying. The 10Y rally (+$0.9B TLT inflow) is real but modest — the market is not yet fully pricing a Hormuz reopening in rates, which suggests further bond rally ahead if the deal closes.

drivers.name: Iran Peace Memorandum — Axios: US close to one-page de-escalation, Trump pauses Project Freedom
drivers.detail: Axios reported the White House believed it was close to a one-page memorandum aimed at de-escalating the Iran conflict. Trump paused Project Freedom — the Hormuz naval escort mission — to provide diplomatic space. The US expects Iranian responses on several key points in the next 48 hours. Nothing signed yet, 'nothing agreed,' but this is the most concrete diplomatic movement since the ceasefire began. WTI -7% to $95.19, Brent below $100. hormuzclosurePct upgraded to 20% (from 12%) as the direction of travel is clearly toward reopening. If the memorandum is signed and Hormuz formally reopens, WTI could fall to $80-85 within days.

drivers.name: Disney Streaming Profitability Milestone — 10.6% margin, first double-digit streaming operating margin
drivers.detail: Disney revenue $25.17B (+7%), adj EPS $1.57 (+8%), streaming operating income +88% to $582M — the first double-digit streaming margin in company history. Parks record fiscal Q2 with revenue $9.49B and operating income $2.62B (+5%). The NY Fed Liberty Street Economics K-shaped consumption data confirms high-income consumers are absorbing the oil shock and maintaining discretionary spending — Disney's customer demographic is exactly this cohort. This is the consumer resilience trade: experiences over goods, even in an energy-shock environment.

drivers.name: K-Shaped Inflation Deepening — Low-income consumers cutting oil consumption, high-income absorbing
drivers.detail: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics published data on the K-shaped gasoline consumption pattern in March 2026. Low-income households: lowest increase in nominal gas spending because they cut consumption most. High-income households: largest jump in spending because they reduced consumption least. This has three implications: (1) consumer staples and value retailers face real demand destruction; (2) premium consumer brands (DIS, luxury, experiences) remain resilient; (3) the PCE basket is being distorted — headline will fall faster if Iran resolves, but core services (which high-income households drive) will remain sticky.

drivers.name: Samsung $1T Market Cap — Second Asian firm after TSMC crosses threshold on AI memory demand
drivers.linked: AI hardware stack, DRAM, HBM, global EM
drivers.detail: Samsung Electronics crossed $1 trillion market cap on Wednesday — joining TSMC as the only two Asian companies at this valuation. The milestone is entirely driven by AI memory demand: Samsung is the second-largest HBM producer after SK Hynix and is racing to close the gap with Micron in AI-grade DRAM. The $1T milestone signals that the AI hardware trade is now global, not just US-listed. South Korea's KOSPI (already +10% on the ceasefire day in April) is positioned as a direct beneficiary of both the AI trade and any Hormuz reopening.

risks.title: Iran deal falls through — memorandum is not a treaty, Trump conditions may be unacceptable to Iran
risks.desc: Axios noted 'nothing has been agreed yet' and cautioned about calling this a done deal. Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei has previously signalled he won't give up nuclear or missile technology. If Iran rejects the memorandum terms, WTI spikes back to $110+ immediately, reversing all of today's energy outflows and triggering a sharp equity selloff. The gap between current market pricing (WTI $95) and break-even pricing (pre-deal WTI $108) is the risk.

risks.title: Nvidia May 20 — Arm's $15B roadmap raises the bar; a clean beat is no longer enough
risks.desc: ARM's $15B chip revenue target by 2031 and AMD's data center +57% have set an extraordinarily high expectation bar for Nvidia's May 20 print. The Palantir template (-7% on a clean beat) applies directly: at 35x+ forward earnings, Nvidia needs a massive blowout — data center >$45B, Q2 guide >$50B — to sustain the multiple. Any guidance conservatism could trigger a 8-12% single-day pullback and risk contagion to the broader semiconductor trade.

risks.title: 30Y remains near 5% — fiscal premium not resolved by Iran deal alone
risks.desc: The 30Y pulled back from 5.02% to 4.98% on oil collapse but is still historically elevated. The fiscal risk premium driving the 30Y is not just about energy inflation — it reflects structural US deficit concerns, Warsh's unknown policy path, and supply dynamics. A Hormuz reopening resolves the energy component but not the fiscal component. 30Y could re-test 5.00% on the next JOLTS/CPI data if Warsh signals hawkish intent at June 17.

risks.title: K-shaped consumer stress — low-income households cutting energy consumption is deflationary but credit-negative
risks.desc: NY Fed data showing low-income households are cutting gasoline consumption significantly is a deflationary signal that helps headline PCE — but it also signals financial stress in the bottom income quintile. Credit card delinquency rates for lower-income borrowers have been rising. If unemployment ticks up as manufacturing remains in contraction (ISM 48.7) and inflation stays elevated, this cohort faces a credit event. BAMLH0A0HYM2 HY spread narrowing (creditTighteningScore 48) but this bears watching.

risks.title: Arm AGI CPU pivot risk — manufacturing transition from IP licensing to chip production is untested
risks.desc: Arm's $15B chip revenue target by 2031 requires successful execution of its first chip manufacturing programme in 35 years. The company has never produced silicon at scale. Morgan Stanley downgraded ARM to Equal-Weight (despite raising PT to $150) citing 'near-term risks as Arm transitions into chip manufacturing.' At 108x+ forward earnings, manufacturing execution risk is fully loaded into the multiple.
